thread:
sasha: Quick sync — I'm opening a small docs PR to add an interactive provisioning walkthrough for Dedicated capacity. Goals: clarify autoscale cooldown vs tenant-affinity, include a migration note for reserved->dedicated label mapping, add Python SDK + CLI samples, and fix the runbook link that 404s. PTAL who can review?

ryan: SG. Can you also include a tiny section on migration gotchas (labels + scalepolicy differences)? We keep getting the same questions in onboarding.

sasha: Yep. Drafted a YAML snippet showing tenant labels + an autoscale policy + fallback. Dropping it here for quick feedback:
```yaml
# dedicated provisioning example
tenant_selector:
  tenant_labels:
    team: "payments"
    env: "prod"
placement:
  affinity: prefer  # prefer-affinity, not a strict pin
autoscale_policy:
  min_replicas: 2
  max_replicas: 20
  cooldown_seconds: 30
fallback:
  when_unavailable: shared_pool
```

lia_docs: Nice! Two micro-nits: 1) prefer `cooldown_seconds` (you already used it, good), 2) add a short sentence explaining `affinity: prefer` ≠ hard isolation. Maybe: "Prefer affinity favors tenant-local placement but may fall back." :+1:

mike_eng: Runtime note — avoid `tenant_selector: deprecated_key` (we still see that in old snippets). Use `tenant_labels` as Sasha did. Also recommend adding a tiny example that shows capacity fallback to shared pool when tenant-local capacity is exhausted. Ops will thank you.

sasha: Added fallback block above. Also put a one-line Python SDK example to make onboarding easy:
```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient()
config = {
  "tenant_labels": {"team": "payments", "env": "prod"},
  "autoscale": {"min_replicas": 2, "max_replicas": 20, "cooldown_seconds": 30}
}
client.provision_dedicated(config)
```

anya: Can we include a quick CLI command too? New SRE hires always ask for CLI copy-paste.

sasha: Sure, added CLI sample:
```
# CLI: provision a dedicated pool for the payments team
redwoodctl dedicated create --labels team=payments,env=prod --min 2 --max 20 --cooldown 30 --fallback shared_pool
```

ryan: Also add a short migration note: teams moving from reserved pools should map `min_instances` -> `min_replicas`, and be warned that tenant-affinity semantics changed (see notes). I'll draft the SLA phrasing about preemption windows (dedicated burst vs reserved) and ping legal.

lia_docs: I hunted down the broken runbook link — PR was pointing to `/docs/provisioning` which 404s. Correct target is `/runbooks/dedicated-provisioning-handbook`. I'll update the anchor and add an inline alias so older links still work.

deploy-bot: Link check: found 1 broken link in PR #4523 -> /docs/provisioning (404). Suggested replacement: /runbooks/dedicated-provisioning-handbook.

sasha: Thanks, pushing branch now: `docs/dedicated/provisioning-walkthrough`. Assigning reviewers @lia_docs @ryan. Plan: merge after runbook link, SDK sample tests, and one quick runtime validation. ETA EOD PT.

ryan: Quick FYI from eng-runtime: prefer `min_replicas` over `min_instances` in examples. Older SDKs (<0.9) still use `min_instances` — maybe add a tiny compatibility note.

sasha: Good call. Added a compatibility paragraph: "If you're on SDK <0.9, use `min_instances` — we map it to `min_replicas` server-side. Upgrade recommended."

lia_docs: LGTM once you add the compatibility note and the fallback sentence. I'll do a final pass for microcopy and link anchors.

sasha: Awesome — merging after your pass. Thanks everyone :rocket:
